full_judgment:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, J: No one appears on behalf of the petitioner as well as on behalf of the opposite party. The Civil Revision is taken up for disposal on merit.

2. This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.04.2002 passed by the learned Additional. District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 20 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 27.11.2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Additional court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 231 of 2000 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem it and proper.

3. The short facts leading to the disposal of the rule is that the opposite party as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 231 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for declaration that the registered kabala deed being No. 4702 dated 04.07.1995 of the Sub-Registrar's Office, Mirpur is illegal, void, malafide and not binding upon the plaintiff and for ejectment of the defendant from the suit land.

4. The plaintiff’s case in short is that the defendant is a licence in the suit land under the plaintiffs; the suit land belonged to Kazi Abdul Wadud who transferred .0650 acres of land to his wife Mr. Shahida Khatun by way of oral gift on 05.12.1970. She entered into an agreement for sale of the suit land with the plaintiff on 10.06.1972 and she delivered the possession of the suit land to the plaintiff on receipt of 1k. 15,000/- as advance. The plaintiff has been in possession in the suit land by constructing Tin shed house and inducted tenant. Abdul Wadud left Bangladesh for Pakistan after Liberation of Bangladesh and he did not return back from Pakistan. Shahida Khatun has been waiting for her husband and was residing at 90-A Jafrabad. Shahida Khatun at last executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the plaintiff being kabala deed No. 20947 dated 303.09.1985 and receipt Tk. 10,000/- as balance money and got his name mutate3d in the Revenue office and paying rent and other taxes.

5. In the year, 1986 one Md. Mohasin claimed the suit land alleging inter alia that one Shahabuddin Ahmed purchased the same from Kazi Abdul Wadud by a registered deed dated 21.09.1979 and Mohasin and Mojib purchased the land from him on 20.07.1981 and the plaintiff was constrained to institute a suit being title Suit No. 17 of 1986 against said Mohasin and Abdul Majid and the suit was decreed on compromise.

6. In the year 1978 the defendant was helpless and distressed condition and have no shelter to reside with his newly married wife and the plaintiff allowed the defendant to reside in the tin shed house in the schedule land with his wife as a licence of the plaintiff. The plaintiff allowed his brother the defendant to enjoy the rents from the another tin shed house and since then the defendant has been enjoying and possessing the suit land as a licence of the plaintiff.

7. During the current survey operation the defendant managed to have recorded the schedule land in his name on the basis of a deed being No. 4702 dated 04.07.1995 executed by Shain Ara and Kazi Abdul Quiyum both son and daughter of kazi Abdul Wadud in favour of the defendant. The plaintiff filed dispute case No. 77 of 1999 before the Assistant Settlement Officer, Mirpur and the settlement Officer after hearing allowed the dispute case and corrected the record in the name of the plaintiff.

8. The plaintiff served legal notice on 12.08.1999 upon the defendant for vacating the schedule land but he denied and hence the case.

9. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement, denying all material allegations that the suit is not maintainable and barred by Limitation and the suit was not properly valued and sufficient stamps. The plaintiff never acquired the suit land and he never possessed the same. The so-called purchased by the plaintiff is nothing but a paper transaction and that was never acted upon. The definite case of the defendant is that Kazi Abdul Wadud acquired the suit land by way of purchased from one Faizuddin by a registered kabala dated 19.08.1963. The local bad people used to cut earth from the land in the dark night as a result said Abdul Wadud engaged the defendant to take after the land. The local bad people wanted to know whether Abdul Wadud had given him any writings as a result Abdul Wadud executed a agreement in favour of the defendant on 24.09.1969 for looking after the land. The defendant used to cultivate the land and had grown se4asonal crops and used to pay 40% of the usufructs to Abdul Wadud and the defendant used to enjoy remaining 60%. The defendant constructed 2 tin shed house in the suit land and inducted tenant therein and used to pay 40% rent to Kazi Abdul Wadud. The wife of Kazi Abdul Wadud died in the year 1970 and after the death of his wife he retired from his service and started living at Mirpur with his children and constructed more tin shed house in the suit land. In the year 1974 the defendant lost his mother and his father got second marriage. The plaintiff in collusion with his step mother had been trying to misappropriate the entire property of his father as a result the defendant uncared displeasure with his family and the defendant permanently started living in the suit land and he got married in the year 1976 and living in the suit land with his family. The plaintiff misapprociated the property of his father and deprived the defendant from his share. The plaintiff created the papers for grabbing the suit land and to harass the defendant. Kazi Abdul Wadud died in the year 1976 leaving behind one son and one daughter and they on 21.09.1989 executed a deed of agreement in favour of defendant and on 31.12.1995 executed a Power of Attorney and on 04.07.1995 executed and registered a saf kabala deed in favour of the defendant. The defendant got his name mutated in the relevant records of rights and obtained electric line, Gas line, water connection in his name. The plaintiff has no right, title in the suit laude and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

10. The plaintiff in order to prove its case examined 3 witnesses including himself as P.W. 1 while the defendant examined 2 witnesses including himself as D.W. 1.

11. The learned Assistant Judge, 1st Additional Court, Dhaka after hearing the parties decreed the suit. The defendant being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 27.11.2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka preferred an Appeal in the court of District Judge, Dhaka being title appeal No. 20 of 2001. The said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court, Dhaka and the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court Dhaka after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal.

12. The learned Trial Judge on perusal of the pleading of the parties and on execution of both oral and documentary evidence P.Ws and DWs was pleased to dismiss the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial judge the plaintiff preferred title appeal No. 20 of 2001 and the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court Dhaka on perusal of the memo of appeal the impugned judgment and decree and on hearing the submissions of the learned Advocate of both sides was pleased to dismissed the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial judge by his judgment and decree dated 15.04.2002. Against which the instant revisional application has been filed before this Hon'ble Court by the plaintiff who obtained the present rule.

13. The learned trial judge on perusal of the pleading of the parties framed as many as 3 issued the issue are one.

14. Whether the plaintiff has right, title and interest in the suit land and the impugned deed No. 4702 dated 04.07.1995 is illegal?

1. Whether the defendant is the licensee under the plaintiff?

2. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to obtain the relief as prayed for?

<u>15. The plaintiff has claimed that he has purchased the suit land from the wife of Kazi Abdul Wadud while the defendant has claimed that he has purchased the suit land from the heirs of Kazi Abdul Wadud. Plaintiff could not prove the oral gift by Kazi Abdul Wadud. Apart from this, he did not formally prove the title deed to which the certified copy has been submitted under Ext. 1. It has become lucid and luculent from the document under Ext. 3 that the plaintiff's title in the suit has already been declared by a competent court in T.S. No. 17 of 1986. Defendant was not party thereto but this very judgment and decree are in the Ken of him but lie does not challenge it. Plaintiff title and possession in the suit land was affirmed by this above mentioned suit. On the other hand, the defendant has also submitted the certified copy of his title deed. He also did not prove his title deed formally. The validity of the judgment and decree in T.S. No. 17 of 1986 is still prevailing unless and until it is being varied set aside or modified by competent court.</u>

<u>16. In view of the above facts and circumstances, it is opined that plaintiff has right, title and interest in the suit land. Hence, the issue is decided in favour of the plaintiff as the defendant’s title deed is illegal. Plaintiff has claimed that the defendant is the licence under him P.W. 2 Md. Shahab Uddin has stated that Syed Abdul Aziz has given permission to his younger brother to live in the suit land. P.W. 3 has also stated that plaintiff gave permission to live in the suit land. In contrast, the defendant claims that he was a caretaker under the original owner Mr. Wadud. He has stated that Kazi Abdul Wadud was in problem as to the suit land because some unscrupulous persons of the locality used to cut away soil from the suit land. That is why he was looking for a caretaker. Defendant happened to meet with him and was appointed as a caretaker in 1969. He has stated that he was a boy of 18/19 years in 1969. Plaintiff denied the same and put the suggestion that he was boy of 10 years at that time. Defendant has also admitted that he is 3 and 4 years younger than plaintiff his full brother. Plaintiff has submitted the certificate of S.S.C. examination Exbt. 6 which reflects the date of birth of plaintiff is 02.02.1956. So, the defendant was a boy of 9/10 years in 1969 mathematically. The story of appointing caretaker of a boy of 9/10 years as to the problematic suit land is unbelievable. The defendant has also submitted a deed as to appointment of caretaker under Ext. A. On the face of this document it seems that it is forged and got up. It is seemed that it is tried to manifest it as an old document by tainting with light lack inkor colour physical condition of this deed does not commence rate with its claimed age. In view of the above facts and circumstances. The learned Court has been constrained to opine that the document of appointing caretaker under Exbt. A is forged and fabricated. Hence, it is decided that the defendant is the licensee of plaintiff the issue is decided in the affirmative of plaintiff.</u>

17. Keeping congruence with the decisions taken in the foregoing issues the trial judge decided the issued in favour of the plaintiff and accordingly the trial judge decreed the suit against the defendant and document the kabala deed No. 4702 is illegal are not binding upon the plaintiff . The trial judge is directed to defendant in after the possession of the suit land within 40 days from this order against the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Judge in Title Appeal No. 20 of 2001 was preferred before the learned District Judge, Dhaka and on transfer the learned District Judge, 9th Court Dhaka heard the appeal and on due consideration of the judgment and decree of the learned trial judge the last court of fact dismissed the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree of the trial vide judgment and decree dated 15.04.2002.

18. On perusal of the impugned judgment and decree of the last court of fact I find both the courts below on due and proper consideration of both oral and documentary evidence on record rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 1 do not find any misreading non reading non consideration of both oral and documentary evidence as adduced by the P.Ws at the time of trial and all the P.Ws have successively proved the plaint case since both the judgments are based on proper appreciation of both oral and documentary evidence on record. I do not find any merit to interfere the concurrent findings of facts as arrived at by both the courts below. In that view of the matter the impugned judgment and decree of the learned Additional District Judge, 9th Court Dhaka, passed in Title Appeal No. 20 of 2001 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 27.11.2000 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 231 of 2000 is hereby affirmed.

19. In the result, the rule is discharged without any order as to cost.

20. The order of stay as granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

21. The office is hereby directed to send back the lower courts record along with a copy of this judgment to the concerned court forthwith for information and necessary action.

End.
